claims.text: Al-rich lightweight HEAs can combine mechanical strength with corrosion resistance and high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Partial ordering of Al-containing clusters during thermomechanical treatment enhances strength.
Partial ordering of Al-containing clusters promotes stable protective oxide and passivating layers.
The proposed starting materials are as-cast, equiatomic or near-equiatomic Al-rich lightweight HEA ingots containing multiple low-density elements.
Different aging temperatures and times can be used to create different extents of short-range order in the same composition.
The relevant oxidative testing range is 700–900 °C.
The structural mediator consists of nanometer-scale Al-rich clusters coherent with the matrix.
Coherent Al-rich clusters generate local lattice distortions.
The local lattice distortions associated with Al-rich clusters pin dislocations.
Al-rich clusters promote the formation of stable passivating oxides.
Short-range ordering of Al-rich domains impedes active slip and dislocation motion, thereby increasing yield strength.
Al-rich ordered domains provide a continuous supply of protective oxides such as Al2O3 at elevated temperature.
A short-range-ordered variant will have higher yield strength than a chemically identical baseline with minimal Al clustering.
A short-range-ordered variant will have lower corrosion current density than the baseline.
A short-range-ordered variant will exhibit slower high-temperature oxide-scale growth than the baseline.
The baseline is a chemically identical alloy processed under a schedule that produces little short-range order or clustering.
Dissolution or transformation of Al-rich clusters eliminates the proposed synergy among strength, corrosion resistance, and oxidation resistance.
Rapid cluster coarsening at high temperature may degrade both strengthening and protective-oxide effects.

If measured differences in short-range order produce no corresponding differences in strength, corrosion resistance, or oxidation performance, the proposed causal role of short-range ordering is falsified.
